acceptanceCriteria: A stub gate that exits nonzero causes the documented command sequence to exit nonzero even when tee writes successfully; a passing gate still retains its full log.
body:
Comprehensive expert audit 2026-09-26, REL-02. Source 2961076fc0b78bfab743578f2ef5c17006be058a.

An operator who executes step 8 as written and checks shell exit status can see success when check-hostile-regressions.sh or make core-n1-replay fails, because tee supplies the pipeline status. This weakens the release gate's fail-closed operational path.

Source: docs/RELEASE-RUNBOOK.md:83

Observed checks: "Pinned runbook uses `script/check-hostile-regressions.sh | tee ...` and `make core-n1-replay ... | tee ...` without pipefail or producer-status capture. `sh -c 'false | tee /dev/null'` returned pipeline_exit=0. The actual hostile and N-1 gates were NOT_RUN by this audit."

Owning contract: "SOP-V0-012; CCF-V1-007"

Correction: Use an explicit Bash pipefail invocation or capture the gate status separately and abort on nonzero; retain the output file only with an explicit PASS verdict.

Report: .agent-evidence/2026-09-26-comprehensive-audit.md; original reports and evidence: .agent-evidence/audit-20260926/. Focused checks plus independent review are required for repair; any native release qualification needs the selected candidate and owner-dispatched run. No qualification or promotion is implied by this ticket.
title: Release runbook pipelines can mask a failed hostile regression or N-1 replay
